SUMMARY

GE Vernova Inc.(GEV-1.34%)reported third quarter results that led management to raise its full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA margin, and free cash flow. Management reported that strong global demand for electricity infrastructure drove a book-to-bill ratio of more than 2-for-1, pushing the total backlog to $197 billion. The company announced the $9 billion acquisition of Trench Group to vertically integrate critical high-voltage grid components and simultaneously doubled its share repurchase authorization to $20 billion. The Power and Electrification segments reported significant margin expansion, while the Wind segment achieved profitability for the quarter following the resolution of litigation and improved service performance.

Operator:Good day, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to GE Vernova's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call.[Operator Instructions]My name is Liz, and I will be your conference coordinator today.[Operator Instructions]As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the program over to your host for today's conference, Michael Lapides, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please proceed.

Michael Lapides:Thank you. Welcome to the conference call on GE Vernova's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings and the planned acquisition of Trench Group. I'm joined today by our CEO, Scott Strazik; and CFO, Ken Parks. Our conference call remarks will include both GAAP and non-GAAP financial results, including the stand-alone forecast of Trench Group. Reconciliations between GAAP and non-GAAP measures can be found in today's press release and presentation slides, both of which are available on our website. Our Trench Group comments reflect expectations for the transaction, the cost and revenue synergies from the transaction and capital allocation plans.

The Trench Group acquisition price and financial information are expressed in U.S. dollar equivalents based on a euro to U.S. dollar exchange rate of $1.12. Actual U.S. dollar equivalent amounts may differ based on the prevailing exchange rate at the applicable times. The Trench Group financial information was prepared by GE Vernova based on data provided by Trench Group and reflect Trench Group's accounting policies, which may differ from GE Vernova's. Please note that unless otherwise specified, our year-over-year commentary or variances on orders, revenue, adjusted and segment EBITDA and margin discussed during our prepared remarks are on an organic basis. We will make forward-looking statements about our performance in the Trench Group business.

These statements are based on how we see things today. While we may elect to update these forward-looking statements at some point in the future, we do not undertake any obligation to do so. As described in our SEC filings, today's press release and presentation slides, all of which are available on our website, actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties. The acquisition is subject to regulatory approvals and standard closing conditions, including information and employee consultation where required. With that, I'll hand the call over to Scott.

Scott Strazik:Thanks, Michael. We have a lot to cover today, but I wanted to start with 3 main messages. First, our growth continues to accelerate with both our core business and new products with almost $30 billion in new orders and an expansion of our backlog from $176 billion to approximately $200 billion in 3Q, we continue to see strong pull from customers for the solutions we offer. This demand is not only for our existing equipment, but also for services, where we saw 10% orders growth in the quarter. We also see growing interest in our new offerings, including in both power with a nuclear SMR and multiple products in electrification, including MV-UPS and solid-state transformers.

Second, our margin expansion is encouraging, but no one inside GEV is satisfied with where we are. This is just the beginning with significant opportunity in all 3 business segments. Power reached 21% EBITDA margins in what is historically our weakest margin quarter as 3Q is typically our lowest quarter for services activity. These margins reflect the first quarter of our 5 gigawatt of gas power equipment shipments at better prices. Electrification reached 19%, EBITDA margins while growing R&D mid-teens to support strong new product introduction opportunities. Wind turned profitable on strong services improvement, and we continue improving execution in offshore as our backlog to complete continues to come down.

Across all 3 businesses and corporate, we have investments in automation and AI with strong use cases that will expand margins over the medium term, but in 3Q in isolation, remain a net expense. Point being, we are early in our margin expansion acceleration. Third, we have delivered significant year-to-date cash generation to end the quarter with approximately $17 billion in cash, and we've been working hard to position GE Vernova to invest this capital for strong returns.

We are pleased to announce the signing of the Trench Group acquisition, which will strengthen our core Electrification offerings in high-voltage grid equipment, be accretive on day 1 and bring us industry-leading technology to innovate into the future and serve this growing market. In parallel with announcing this $9 billion acquisition, we are announcing a doubling of our stock buyback program from $10 billion to $20 billion. After investing $1.6 billion in the buyback in 3Q and over $1.3 billion in October, we have largely completed our $10 billion authorization with excellent returns, having acquired 15.6 million shares at an average price of approximately $635. It is early in our journey.

We remain humble, but we have real conviction that we are building a unique company to serve the growing market and deliver for our shareholders for the long term. With that, I'd like to go to the next page and give an overview of the Trench acquisition. The announcement today of our acquisition of the Trench Group is an important step forward in strengthening and scaling our Electrification business in the high and medium voltage markets globally. If I take a step back, the beginning of '25, there were 2 assets of scale I felt we needed in electrification.

The first was Prolec to expand our North America manufacturing footprint and to simplify the front-end commercial experience for our end customers, especially the hyperscalers. And the second is Trench for the technology differentiation, management team and the importance of the components Trench provides and solutions we deliver today. There are many factors driving our conviction in the high-voltage market for the long term. Data centers require large electricity loads, driving an increasing need for more efficient high-voltage equipment. Trench, as an example, has secured multiple agreements with hyperscalers in the past 2 years. In addition, global utilities are also building out more high-voltage infrastructure.

Today's grid loses as much as 8% from power generation to end use and the upgrade of the grid to higher voltages dramatically reduces energy losses, making the whole grid more economical. In addition, as the existing grid takes on more load with increased building electrification, manufacturing growth, heat pumps and EVs, grid reinforcements to higher voltages will be required. And in parts of the world building significant wind and solar, there is a need to transport electrons over long distances at higher voltages to eliminate waste.

India is a great example of this today and is a market where we are demonstrating real commercial success, including our announced win on the Barmer HVDC project that will be a $1.5 billion order in 4Q. Trench further positions us to serve this global high-voltage market opportunity we project to be $130 billion by the end of the decade. As an existing supplier to Vernova, Trench is a business we know well. It's complementary and differentiated technology for high-voltage solutions will broaden our grid equipment portfolio and expand our presence across product lines where we have a modest presence today.

Vertically integrating Trench will also give us greater capacity and certainty across a key part of the supply chain, strengthening our ability to deliver for customers. The foundation of Trench's success is technical excellence and a strong management team. With more than 3,000 highly skilled employees across 11 factories, Trench has established a footprint in many of the world's largest grid markets. These capabilities have enabled Trench to develop deep, trusted relationships with a broad customer base serving utilities, grid operators and increasingly hyperscalers.

We expect this transaction to close late '27 and with a $9 billion purchase price, we are paying 13x '28 EBITDA before synergies, the first full year we expect Trench to be included in our financial results. This is a strategically compelling and attractive acquisition that is directly aligned with our capital allocation priorities. We will add scale to the core of our fast-growing Electrification segment to better serve the global electricity super cycle. Turning to the next page. You can see on the left-hand side the estimated '26 revenue of Trench and GE Vernova with the 3 primary product lines in the Trench portfolio.

Trench revenue in '26 is estimated at $1.4 billion and similar to our Electrification business is projected to grow at double-digit levels over the coming years to approach $2 billion of revenue in '28 after the expected close. I'd like to provide a bit more context and color on each of the product lines. Every medium and high-voltage transformer has a bushing for insulation and mechanical support used for reliable grid connection. Today, we source most of our bushings externally.

But tomorrow, we will be able to internalize this key technology within the Trench facilities and better serve our customers with improved cycle time and integrated performance as we continue to invest in this business, just as we are doing with Prolec, which you see very clearly in the growth of our Prolec results. In many cases, customers specify the bushing provider for large transformers, and we see opportunities where Trench bushings are the preferred technology to better integrate our transformer product line to drive commercial synergies. Post close, we will source a much larger percentage of bushings for our transformers from the Trench factories to deliver better outcomes for our customers.

Instrument transformers are important high-voltage equipment in electrical substations, typically greater than 35 kV that are used to measure voltage and provide protection. This equipment is utilized for new build high-voltage electrical substations, for instance, with data centers where you see us playing a significant role, but this is also technology to support upgrades as existing infrastructure extends past its useful life. In the U.S. alone, we project over 55,000 transmission substations will be completely rebuilt or upgraded to higher voltages in the next decade. Point being, our opportunity is both in expanding and modernizing the existing grid and serving new growth with opportunities like data centers. And finally, medium and high-voltage coils.

This equipment connects to the substation and stores electrical energy inside a magnetic field to enhance grid reliability and power quality. The innovative high-voltage technology Trench produces is directly aligned with where customers are investing and where we see long-term demand continuing to grow. We are very confident these technologies will allow us to better serve our customers, which I'll go into in more detail on the next page. We talked in the past how our existing addressable market in electrification is projected to reach $300 billion by 2030. The high-voltage equipment market is an estimated $130 billion of the $300 billion.

And you can see on the left-hand side of this page how each product line inside Trench supports our offerings across the columns. We see the high-voltage equipment market continue to grow at high single digits for the long term, driven by the macro factors I mentioned on the earlier page. The real message on this page is we have a great conviction that customers will benefit significantly with our addition of Trench to the product portfolio to deliver to them more optimized, integrated solutions. This will also provide our customers a more seamless experience and increase our capabilities in delivering sustainable solutions our customers value today.

For instance, Trench is the leader in dry type bushings, an increasingly important technology across power transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems, substations and stability solutions. Dry type transformers use a resin instead of oil, which reduces maintenance, is better for the environment and dramatically reduces the risk of fire. Our combined global manufacturing footprint will be a key differentiator, enhancing delivery and lead time management. With Trench, we will strengthen our ability to support the development of higher voltage electrical systems globally, including the build-out of 765 kV transmission in the U.S. As we continue to serve Trench's existing customers, we can also extend Trench's products to regions with significant electrical infrastructure needs for customers that we serve today.

Finally, Trench's track record in quality and delivery aligns directly with our own and positions us to better serve customers' rising demand for grid equipment. Turning to the next slide. I want to put in context how this acquisition supports our existing Electrification businesses. Today, we have a $46 billion backlog, which, again, to remind everyone, was $7 billion at the start of '22. Our 2 largest businesses, Grid Systems Integration and Power Transmission will be the largest direct beneficiaries on day 1 of the acquisition. Although longer term, we also see a positive impact on our power conversion and storage business, especially within new products we're developing like the MV-UPS stability block.

GSI delivers HVDC projects and AC substations for utilities and data centers, among other high-voltage solutions. Today, we source some of the components for these offerings externally, including from Trench, which supply the majority of HVDC lines globally. Going forward, we will be able to offer better integrated solutions using technologically advanced products that improve system durability and are demanded by customers to grow our GSI business at attractive margins. In Power Transmission, which produces transformers, switchgear and capacitors, Trench will provide scale through its bushings and instrument transformers. Bushings are a key component used in our power transformers and Trench's differentiated technology will help to deliver high-voltage transformers to customers.

Lead times across the industry are increasingly important, and this transaction will enhance supply chain certainty for both businesses within Electrification. By bringing Trench's manufacturing footprint and capabilities inside Vernova, we expect greater visibility into production planning and improved ability to align this component supply with our customers' project schedules. Finally, Trench is adding significant capacity across its 11 factories globally to meet rising demand. This includes Trench's newly opened factory in North Carolina, which will be the first U.S. manufacturer of high-voltage bushings up to 765 kV, expanding Trench's leadership in extra high-voltage technology and giving us an important capability within our U.S. footprint.

With Trench, we will have additional scale in key geographies and more flexibility to serve customers, complementing our existing and planned capacity across Electrification. Taken together, Trench enhances our Electrification segment's ability to deliver. As you will see in our 3Q results on the subsequent pages, our core businesses continue to gain momentum with accelerating growth and margin expansion. The Prolec acquisition is outperforming our expectations and Trench is the right next step in creating an industry-leading electrification business at attractive economics, serving our customers with a team and technology we love. With that, I'll hand it over to Ken to walk through the financial details.

Kenneth Parks:Thanks, Scott. On Slide 9, let me highlight the financial profile of Trench Group and our expectations for the next few years before synergies and integration costs. Trench has strong fundamentals and approximately $5 billion in combined backlog and framework agreements as of September 2026, which has grown over the past several years. Trench has approximately 80 existing framework agreements, some extending into the 2030s, representing volume commitments that account for approximately half of the $5 billion. We expect Trench to generate mid-teens revenue growth annually from 2026 to 2028. As Scott mentioned, this revenue growth is supported by planned capacity expansions.

The majority of the CapEx for these expansions will be completed prior to our anticipated close in late 2027. We also expect Trench to deliver strong margins, including an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 36% in 2028. Even before synergies, this is an immediately accretive transaction. As Scott noted, we currently plan to fund the $9 billion acquisition price using an equal mix of debt and cash on hand and remain committed to maintaining an investment-grade balance sheet. Even after issuing roughly $4.5 billion in debt resulting from the acquisition, we expect to remain below a 1x debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio. Turning to Slide 10.

I'll walk through the synergy opportunities we see in this transaction, which are reinforced by the proven execution and value creation we've demonstrated in the integration of Prolec that is already well underway and performing ahead of expectations. Starting with cost synergies. We plan to apply our combined advanced manufacturing expertise, including robotics and automation across the expanded footprint. We'll expand lean to increase volume and capture efficiencies by redesigning and enhancing floor layouts to improve yields and factory flow. We'll also bring together the sourcing operations of Trench and GE Vernova to drive efficiency in the aggregated material spend. And finally, we see potential to optimize the production cost of these offerings through the use of best cost locations.

On revenue, we see growth opportunities across GE Vernova and Trench's combined and highly complementary customer base. This is especially true for utilities and hyperscalers in North America. In 2026, Trench saw significant growth in its hyperscaler business, and our strong track record of partnering with these customers positions us well to continue serving their evolving needs. We also plan to use our existing commercial capabilities in markets like India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East to expand Trench's reach and grow revenues. For example, India is one of Asia's largest HVDC markets and its electrical system increasingly relies on high and extra high-voltage grid equipment.

We'll utilize Trench's offerings, combined with our existing capabilities in India to serve this opportunity, especially as we evaluate expanding manufacturing of Trench's products there. In summary, we expect to realize approximately $50 million to $100 million of annualized cost synergies by 2030, and we see additional revenue synergy potential over time. As we move forward, we will stay focused on both a disciplined integration and execution to deliver on the opportunities we've outlined today. With that, let me turn it back to Scott.

Scott Strazik:Thanks, Ken. Put simply, Trench strengthens our offerings in high-voltage grid equipment, expands our scale in key product categories and improves our ability to serve customers as global demand for electrification continues to grow. With approximately $5 billion in combined backlog and framework agreements, Trench has strong visibility into its long-term growth and earnings profile. This is an attractive acquisition that will be immediately accretive after closing. Our Electrification team continues to deliver solid results with '26 representing another year of increasing backlog, growing revenues and expanding margins. The Prolec integration is performing ahead of expectations, and we are successfully driving both revenue and cost synergies.

We expect Prolec integration to be substantially complete before Trench closes, and this experience reinforces our confidence in our ability to integrate Trench with that same discipline and focus. Finally, this acquisition is fully aligned with our capital allocation priorities, which include investing for organic growth, returning capital to shareholders and pursuing targeted M&A in our core businesses where we can add scale, increase vertical integration and accelerate R&D. Trench fits that framework very well, and we're doing this all while returning significant capital to shareholders and maintaining a strong balance sheet. Now with that, let's shift to our 3Q results on Page 13.

Throughout ' 26, demand for our solutions has continued to strengthen, and our teams are executing well to meet customers' growing energy needs. So far, we have added $46 billion to our total backlog to reach approximately $200 billion with a margin profile that continues to improve. In '26, we expect the growth in equipment margin and backlog to be substantially larger than that of '25, which was approximately $8 billion at improved margin rates, positioning us well to drive further margin expansion and cash generation in the years to come. As we grow our large installed base, we will generate additional services growth at high margins.

This year alone, we've seen 17% growth in services orders with services backlog up $7 billion. We are running the business better today with solid execution across our 3 segments. In Power, we continue to see strong global demand for our equipment and services. In Gas Power, we've signed 52 gigawatts of new agreements year-to-date and now expect at least 130 gigawatts under contract by the end of '26 compared to 83 gigawatts when we started the year. In '27, we expect our combined gigawatts under contract and our Gas Power equipment backlog to continue to grow.

In 3Q, we shipped 5 gigawatts while signing 11 gigawatts of orders and slot reservation agreements to grow our total gigawatts under contract from 116 to 122 gigawatts sequentially. This includes orders for 55 heavy-duty units and 57 aeroderivatives. As expected, we've reached an important inflection point where backlog is now greater than our SRA balance, further reinforcing the certainty that we will ship more gigawatts through the rest of the decade. This quarter, we sold multiple slots for '32 delivery as the demand environment remains strong and customers secure turbines further into the future. Demand also remains diverse with approximately 100 customers in 25 different countries, of which approximately 80% are traditional customers and 20% are for data centers.

We are seeing strong equipment pricing and total life cycle economics in gas. On the equipment side, 3Q orders were priced more than 20% above 4Q '25 equipment orders based on higher-priced turbines and a greater mix of aeroderivatives. Given our view of SRA conversions, we expect gas equipment orders to have a price per kW in 4Q that is lower than 3Q due to fewer aeroderivatives and relatively more 50-hertz units. Full year '26 gas orders pricing per KW will be approximately 50% higher than full year '25 orders. Our large and growing installed base will generate services growth at higher margins for years to come, increasing in the 30s as these units are installed.

Our HA fleet running or on contract will be at least 400 units by the end of '27. And as I mentioned at a recent conference, we expect every gigawatt of HAs to generate $0.5 billion of high-margin services revenue over the first 20 years of its lifetime. It's not just gas where we're seeing services growth. More customers are coming to our nuclear business for uprates and life extensions as our equipment touches 65 gigawatts of the U.S. nuclear fleet. In Electrification, backlog growth is being driven by both traditional customers and data centers with equipment backlog rising by $12 billion in '26 so far.

Total segment data center orders are now more than $6 billion year-to-date, including roughly $1.4 billion in 3Q. As mentioned earlier, Prolec is performing well, and we're encouraged by the continued strong momentum we are seeing in this business's integration and the capabilities it brings to better serve our customers, especially in North America. In '26 so far, we have booked $900 million in orders for transformers in the U.S. that will be fulfilled by our global factories, something we could not do when we did not fully own Prolec. In Wind, the team has remained focused on execution this year to reach profitability in 3Q despite a softer U.S. market for new onshore equipment.

This year, we have continuously driven onshore services margin expansion versus a year ago. While the U.S. market for new onshore equipment remains soft, we are monitoring the outcome of 232 tariffs that impact wind development, which should lead to more orders clarity. In offshore, we are making good progress on Dogger Bank and are pleased that we closed out the open dispute with Vineyard Wind in 3Q with a very modest negative P&L impact. We are focused on investing to deliver innovative solutions for profitable growth. We have spent $2.4 billion in R&D and CapEx so far in '26, reinvesting nearly as much back in the business as in all of '25.

Let me give you a few examples of where our investments are leading to new business and commercial opportunities. In nuclear, we continue advancing the SMR for industrialization at scale as evidenced by our continued progress on the existing project underway in Ontario. The recent approval by the NRC for the construction permit at Clinch River is a significant milestone for TVA, GE Vernova Hitachi and the U.S. nuclear industry as the country advances towards a new generation of nuclear power deployment with SMRs. We also won a 1.2 gigawatt tech select for our SMR in Sweden in 3Q, building momentum in Europe. In Electrification, this includes commercializing multiple new solutions like energy management system, MV-UPS and solid-state transformers.

We recently signed our first MV-UPS order with a hyperscaler as well as several EMS orders this year. We are also making good progress developing SSTs with hyperscalers, and we already have our first prototype in testing now in our facility in Malta, New York. Additionally, we have already received notification of a hyperscaler award for our 6-megawatt outdoor SST and will advance contracting in 4Q. We are operating from a position of financial strength and are well positioned to serve and transform the global electricity system. We're actively improving how we operate and generating better returns while expanding the platform of solutions we provide customers as their need for infrastructure accelerates.

Given the strength of third quarter performance and confidence in our fourth quarter trajectory, we are raising our revenue, margin and free cash flow guidance for '26. With that, I will turn the call over to Ken for more details on our 3Q performance as well as our financial outlook.

Kenneth Parks:Thanks, Scott. Turning to Slide 14. We delivered strong results in the third quarter with robust orders, growing backlog and revenues, margin expansion and significant free cash flow generation. In the quarter, we booked orders of $29.3 billion, a 96% increase year-over-year and a book-to-bill ratio of more than 2x with growth in both equipment and services. As Scott mentioned, our backlog expanded to $197 billion, a significant year-over-year and sequential increase. Equipment backlog increased to $104 billion, up approximately $16 billion sequentially and 92% year-over-year, driven by both Power and Electrification and incorporates Prolec's backlog. Equipment backlog margin continues to expand, reflecting favorable price and our continued focus on disciplined underwriting.

Our services backlog grew approximately $11 billion or 14% year-over-year to $93 billion, led by Power. As Scott touched on, the growth in our installed base will continue to generate strong services growth at high margins. Revenue increased 18%. Equipment revenue rose 26% year-over-year as 65% growth at Power and 21% growth at Electrification was partially offset by anticipated lower Wind revenues. Services revenue increased 6% year-over-year with growth in onshore wind and power. Price remained positive. Adjusted EBITDA grew 123% year-over-year to $1.9 billion, led by Power and Electrification. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 690 basis points with higher price, more profitable volume and further productivity more than offsetting inflation.

We completed our exit from transition services agreements with GE Aerospace in the quarter, an important milestone as we successfully concluded a multiyear effort to build the stand-alone capabilities required to operate independently. This work not only completes an important part of the separation, but will also drive approximately $135 million of G&A savings, of which approximately $100 million has been realized to date. This strong adjusted EBITDA and working capital management drove $5.4 billion of free cash flow in the third quarter. Working capital was a $5.3 billion cash benefit, driven primarily by down payments on increased orders and slot reservations at Power as well as down payments at Electrification.

Year-over-year, free cash flow increased $4.7 billion, driven by higher positive benefits from working capital and stronger adjusted EBITDA, partially offset by higher taxes and CapEx investments supporting capacity expansion. We also made a voluntary payment of approximately $350 million to fund retiree benefits and transfer the obligation to a third-party insurer. The transaction generated an $84 million gain, which is removed from our adjusted EBITDA results. With our strong cash position, we'll continue to seek opportunities to utilize cash proactively when those opportunities generate solid economic returns.

We ended 3Q with a cash balance of approximately $17 billion, a $4 billion increase from the end of the second quarter after returning $1.8 billion of cash to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends in the quarter. Under our repurchase program, we've repurchased 15.6 million shares at an average price of $635 per share, totaling approximately $9.9 billion through October 23. Importantly, with the $10 billion increase in our share repurchase authorization, we'll continue to be disciplined in returning capital to shareholders and remain committed to maintaining a strong investment-grade balance sheet. We're encouraged by our strong financial performance in the third quarter.

Our growing backlog with increasing margin continues to provide an excellent foundation for further improvement in our financial performance moving forward. Now turning to Power on Slide 15. The segment delivered another strong quarter with robust demand, strong revenue growth and solid EBITDA margin expansion. Power orders more than doubled as gas power equipment increased by approximately 4x year-over-year on higher volume and pricing from both HA and aeroderivative units. Power services orders increased 12%, driven by Gas Power and Nuclear Power. Revenue increased 25%. Equipment revenue increased primarily from Gas Power, driven by higher turbine volume and favorable price. We shipped a total of 32 gas turbines in the quarter, a 60% increase year-over-year, including 13 aeroderivatives.

Services revenue also increased due to growth at Gas Power and Nuclear Power. EBITDA margins expanded 830 basis points to 21.4%, mainly driven by favorable price and higher volume more than offsetting inflation as well as additional expenses to support capacity investments at gas as well as R&D. For the full year, we're raising our organic revenue growth expectations from 18% to 20% to 19% to 21% due to higher volume, including aeroderivatives. Given the improved volume, we're also raising our Power EBITDA margin range by 2 points from 17% to 19% to 19% to 21%. Turning to Electrification on Slide 16. We had another quarter of significant backlog and revenue growth as well as EBITDA margin expansion.

Orders remained strong, reaching $5.4 billion at roughly 1.4x revenue. While we saw significant growth in substations and switchgear, total orders decreased 9% year-over-year due to a significant order for $1.6 billion of synchronous condensers in Saudi Arabia in the third quarter of 2025. Equipment orders growth was particularly strong in North America, doubling year-over-year. North America, which includes Prolec backlog, continues to be the largest portion of our Electrification equipment backlog, while all regions, including Europe, are still growing. Importantly, Electrification equipment orders continued outpacing revenue and further increased our equipment backlog to $42 billion, up 60% or roughly $16 billion compared to the third quarter of 2025.

Revenue increased 51% on a reported basis, inclusive of Prolec and 16% organically with growth across all regions. We saw increased volume at grid systems integration, primarily from substations and HVDC equipment and at Power Transmission, primarily from switchgear and transformers. Prolec also delivered solid performance with almost $950 million of revenue. Electrification segment EBITDA was $739 million, increasing by 57% year-over-year with margin expansion of 470 basis points to 19.1%, led by strong volume, productivity and favorable pricing. For the full year, we continue to expect revenue at Electrification to be between $14.5 billion to $15 billion.

In addition, we now expect Electrification EBITDA margin to trend towards the higher end of the 18% to 20% range as the team continues to deliver solid execution. Turning to Slide 17 on Wind. We delivered a profitable quarter as we make good progress executing our strategy. In the third quarter, the team continued to deliver improving performance in onshore wind services while making good progress on Dogger Bank B installations and commissioning. Wind orders increased 16% with growth in onshore equipment and services, especially for repowering in North America. It remains difficult to call an inflection point in U.S. orders as customers still face permitting delays and tariff uncertainty.

Wind revenue increased 3% in the quarter due to higher onshore services and offshore equipment driven by higher deliveries and installations at Dogger Bank B, partially offset by lower onshore equipment deliveries. Wind delivered EBITDA of $72 million. The year-over-year improvement in EBITDA was primarily due to lower offshore project costs and improved onshore wind performance, including recoveries of previously paid tariffs and better services, partially offset by lower onshore equipment volume. For the full year, we now anticipate organic revenue to be down mid-single digits, better than our previous expectation of down low double digits due to additional onshore wind turbine deliveries in the second half of the year.

We now expect EBITDA losses to be between $400 million and $500 million for the year. Significant performance improvement in onshore services has enabled us to accelerate scheduled maintenance from 2027 into the fourth quarter. These incremental service costs, along with the Vineyard Wind settlement more than offset the impact of additional onshore volume. Moving now to Slide 18 to discuss 2026 GE Vernova guidance. Based on our strong year-to-date results and full year segment expectations, we're raising our GE Vernova financial guidance. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $46.5 billion to $47.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA margin to be in the range of 13.5% to 14.5%.

In addition, we also anticipate our free cash flow to be in the range of $16 billion to $17 billion. We're generating significant margin expansion and cash flow this year while still investing in the business. Our 2026 guidance includes a more than 30% year-over-year combined increase in R&D and CapEx as we accelerate our work to support innovation and growth. At corporate, costs are typically uneven across quarters due to compensation timing and portfolio activity at our Financial Services business. We continue to expect full year 2026 corporate costs to be between $450 million and $500 million as we continue investing in AI, robotics and automation to drive productivity over the medium and long term.

For the fourth quarter, we expect growth in revenue and adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin expansion and positive free cash flow. We have delivered strong results year-to-date. The combination of rising demand with consistently stronger execution, investments into our business, the completion of the acquisition of Prolec and the announced acquisition of Trench sets us up nicely going forward. With that, I'll turn it back to Scott.

Scott Strazik:Thanks, Ken. We delivered another strong quarter, and I'm proud of how our teams continue to execute as demand for electricity infrastructure accelerates around the world. With a growing backlog at improving margins, our potential continues to grow, and we are deploying capital, both organically and through M&A with Prolec and Trench to generate strong returns, all while returning significant capital to our shareholders.
